title: S3OD: Towards Generalizable Salient Object Detection with Synthetic Data
claim: Training on large-scale synthetic data yields diverse, high-quality labels and models that generalize to real images, including ambiguous scenes.
layout: 2 stacked rows: image/mask gallery on top, predictions below, dashed divider
description: A two-row gallery with no diagrams or text beyond the row labels. The top row, labeled 'Synthetic Dataset', shows four pairs of a generated photo-realistic image and its white-on-black salient mask. The scenes are huskies pulling a sled, a dinosaur skeleton on a forklift, an ornate iron gate in a room, and a basketball dunker. A dashed line separates the rows. The bottom row, labeled 'Model Predictions', shows real-world images, each with two stacked predicted masks on the right. The images are a golden naga statue, pigeons, a boy with a hoop, a trumpet, a soccer player and a carved chair. The two masks show alternative hypotheses, for example one with and one without the second pigeon or the ball. The eye goes first to the colorful photos, then to the crisp silhouettes.
caption: S3OD Top: Our large-scale synthetic dataset, consisting of diverse complex scenes and high-quality samples. Bottom: Model Predictions. Our model trained on synthetic data generalizes well to real-world images, handling ambiguous scenes by predicting alternative hypotheses.
abstract: Salient object detection exemplifies data-bounded tasks where expensive pixel-precise annotations force separate model training for related subtasks like DIS and HR-SOD. We present a method that dramatically improves generalization through large-scale synthetic data generation and ambiguity-aware architecture. We introduce S3OD, a dataset of over 139,000 high-resolution images created through our multi-modal diffusion pipeline that extracts labels from diffusion and DINO-v3 features. The iterative generation framework prioritizes challenging categories based on model performance. We propose a streamlined multi-mask decoder that handles the inherent ambiguity in salient object detection by predicting multiple valid interpretations. Models trained only on synthetic data achieve 20-50% error reduction in cross-dataset generalization, while fine-tuned versions reach state-of-the-art performance across DIS and HR-SOD benchmarks.
